ON tools.allow -- this is the ONLY guard that was measured to work.
On 2026-09-01 an MCP server projected with codex.agents: ["researcher"]
still reached main. An agent WITHOUT an explicit allow list gets every tool
the gateway has, MCP tools included. Every agent therefore carries one, and
'main' is in this file for that reason alone.

_why: The default agent, and the one an inbound Signal message lands on --
the channel is live and main has no routing rules, so it answers.
It was measured dormant on 2026-09-01: two sessions in three months,
and the only tools it ever called were memory_search and cron.
Its workspace is the shared, hand-made one. The rollout does not touch
those files -- only the tool surface, which until now was all 24 tools
including exec, with sandbox.mode off, reachable from a phone.

_why_model: Nominal, not a measurement: the provider name points at a port, and the
weights behind it are whatever llama-server currently holds. Read the
live profile from llm-switch/current.json, never from this string or
_why_skills: An explicit list REPLACES the inherited default rather than adding to
it, so this also drops the twelve bundled skills (canvas, meme-maker,
weather, ...) that were sitting in its prompt without ever being used.
_why_tools: Named one by one rather than as mora02__*, so that what this agent can
do is readable here without resolving a glob against a running server.
There is no resume, approve or cancel tool -- not because the model is
asked to behave, but because the surface has no such verb (pillar 6).
web_search and web_fetch stay absent: they send data out of the house,
which is its own open question.
